headline: Guernica was bombed in April, the Hindenburg burned in May, and Japan took Nanjing in December
texture: German and Italian aircraft bombed Guernica on April 26 for the Nationalists, and Picasso finished the painting about it by June. The Hindenburg caught fire coming in to land in New Jersey on May 6, in front of newsreel cameras, which ended passenger airships. Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan disappeared over the Pacific on July 2 after taking off from New Guinea.

Japanese troops moved on Nanjing from October 3, began the battle for it on December 1, and occupied the city on December 13. Hitler held a secret meeting in the Reich Chancellery on November 5 to tell his commanders what he intended. The Golden Gate Bridge opened on May 27.

MGM had four of the five biggest films, led by Saratoga, which Jean Harlow died partway through making. Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs opened on December 21 as the first feature-length cel-animated film, and did not reach most of the country until the following year. The Life of Emile Zola won Best Picture. George Gershwin and Maurice Ravel both died this year.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the minimum wage series starts next year and the other two later still. Gershwin and Ravel carry no date because the source lists them as undated sub-entries. Jean Harlow dying during production of Saratoga, and the Hindenburg fire ending passenger airship travel, are general knowledge of those subjects rather than claims from the year pages.
